problem:
Two snowplows are approaching a maintenance station $T$ along perpendicular roads. Snowplow $E$ drives due south toward $T$ at $24\,\text{mph},$ while snowplow $F$ drives due west toward $T$ at $10\,\text{mph}.$ When snowplow $F$ is $6\,\text{miles}$ from $T$ and snowplow $E$ is $8\,\text{miles}$ from $T$, how fast is the distance between the snowplows decreasing? Round your answer to the **nearest integer** and assume that the rate of decreasing distance is **positive**.

The speed of convergence of the two snowplows is approximately
{{field-1}} $\text{mph}.$
worked_solution:
We start by drawing a diagram of the situation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14066033/assets/1109f4736ddfa81344d545802438588967aa18aac379c75a6b7be58688fb931f.png)

In the diagram:

- $x$ is the distance between snowplow $F$ and the maintenance station $T$

- $y$ is the distance between snowplow $E$ and the maintenance station $T$

- $z$ is the distance between the snowplows.

Both snowplows are moving toward $T$, so the leg rates are negative:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dx}{dt} & =-10\text{ }\text{mph} \\ \frac{dy}{dt} & =-24\text{ }\text{mph}\end{aligned}
$$

First, compute $z$ using the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {6}^{2}+{8}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ 36+64 & ={z}^{2} \\ {z}^{2} & =100 \\ z & =10\text{ }\text{mi}\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiate ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ and substitute the known values:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt} & =2z\frac{dz}{dt} \\ 2(6)(-10)+2(8)(-24) & =2(10)\frac{dz}{dt} \\ -120-384 & =20\frac{dz}{dt} \\ -504 & =20\frac{dz}{dt} \\ \frac{dz}{dt} & ≈-25\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

So, the speed of convergence of the two snowplows is approximately $25\text{ }\text{mph}.$
